area: Uptime and performance hardening of the running system (Orlok node) + fleet-wide video resolution consistency. Full report: /tmp/v11-uptime-perf.md

findings.title: Webcam 'apply device' writes an ExecStart override that destroys the self-healing mjpg launcher
findings.evidence: Lines 556-575 build override.conf with 'ExecStart=' + a full mjpg_streamer command using a bare devicePath (fallback '/dev/video0', q85 default at line 554), write it to /etc/systemd/system/mjpg-streamer.service.d/override.conf and restart the unit. scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh header documents the 2026-08-17 incident: a USB re-enumeration crash-looped the unit 42+ times against a hardcoded /dev/video0; the launcher resolves /dev/v4l/by-id at every start to prevent exactly this. systemctl cat mjpg-streamer confirms no override.conf exists on Orlok today, so the trap is armed but unsprung.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator presses Apply in the webcam setup UI during show prep; override.conf replaces the launcher with a bare /dev/videoN path; weeks later a USB over-current blip re-enumerates the camera mid-show and mjpg-streamer crash-loops (Restart=on-failure RestartSec=2, forever) against a dead node — monitoring feed gone until a human edits systemd files.
findings.fix: Rewrite applyDeviceToService to emit /etc/default/monsterbox-cam (MB_CAM_DEV/MB_CAM_RES/MB_CAM_FPS/MB_CAM_Q — the launcher already sources it at lines 16-24) and restart the unit; never emit an ExecStart= replacement. Default quality to 60, matching the launcher.
findings.blast_radius: All six characters (same controller ships fleet-wide); silently reintroduces the 42-crash-loop failure mode on every node where the button is ever pressed.

findings.title: Head-tracking pan-servo claim leaks on tracker crash and is held while driving is refused
findings.evidence: (a) tracker.on('exit') at lines 424-428 only deletes activeTrackers/trackingStatus — no releaseServo; the release exists only in stopMotionTrackingInternal (lines 347-352), whose comment describes the exact frozen-head failure being guarded. (b) maybeDriveHead claims the servo at lines 663-670 BEFORE the calibrated-window guardrail check; line 591 refusal warn appears 610x in /var/log/monsterbox.err while monsterbox.log has 1,828 'DENIED claim on servo 15 by idle-loop' and 1,826 'IdleLoop All servos preempted, pausing' lines — the claim is held at priority 80 while nothing drives.
findings.failure_scenario: Python tracker crashes on its own (camera unplug, OpenCV error) mid-show: exit handler runs, claim stays held forever, head is frozen out of tracking AND idle/ambient motion until the operator disables head tracking or restarts the server. Separately, with an uncalibrated window the head sits statue-still all night while the UI shows tracking active — and the refusal reason is only in .err.
findings.fix: Call releaseServo(panServoId, headOwner(webcamId)) in the tracker 'exit' handler; move (or add) the guardrail null-check before claimServo in maybeDriveHead.
findings.blast_radius: Any character with head tracking enabled; converts a transient camera/python fault into an all-night frozen head.
findings.characters_affected: 3 (Orlok, servo 15 — currently in the refusing state per 610 .err warns), plus any node with head tracking

findings.title: Video resolution has four disagreeing sources of truth; UI advertises 1080p30 while the stream is VGA15
findings.evidence: arducam-b0205 defaults declare 1920x1080@30 q90; scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh defaults (and the live process, verified via ps: '-r 640x480 -f 15 -q 60') are 640x480@15 q60 per the operator's 2026-08-17 spec; webcamController.js:552-554 apply-path defaults q85; data/character-5/parts.json:33-34 bakes 1920x1080@30; goblin/goblin-pi.js:222 forces ffplay '-vf scale=1920:1080' on a Pi3B. Measured camera cost at VGA15 with an active client: 3 jiffies over 5s = ~0.6% of one core (native MJPEG passthrough).
findings.failure_scenario: Any path that honors the model/part defaults (apply button, a future model-defaults push, character-5 coming out of storage) silently jumps the stream to 1080p30 q90 — ~9x USB bandwidth on a bus shared with the audio adapter and ReSpeaker, for a phone-viewed feed; goblin Pi3B burns CPU software-scaling every frame to 1080p.
findings.fix: Canonical geometry: 640x480@15 q60. Single source of truth: scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh defaults (git-tracked, reaches all six characters via npm run deploy:all, including the four offline nodes on next deploy), per-node override only via /etc/default/monsterbox-cam. Align in-code now: webcam_models.json arducam defaults -> 640x480/15/60, apply path -> env-file writer with q60, character-5 parts.json -> 640x480/15, goblin-pi.js -> drop the scale filter.
findings.blast_radius: All six characters; consistency is exactly what Aaron asked for and today only Orlok's live process matches the spec.
findings.characters_affected: all (1-6); character-5 config provably wrong in-repo

findings.title: performance-history.json is fully rewritten every 5 minutes: ~427 MB/day of SD writes, non-atomic
findings.evidence: recordPerformanceSnapshot (lines 120-142) reads the whole file, appends one snapshot, and rewrites the entire file with plain fs.writeFile; server.js:885 schedules it every 300,000 ms; retention is 30 days and the file is still growing. Measured now: data/performance-history.json = 1,483,408 bytes. 1.48 MB x 288/day ≈ 427 MB/day — larger than all logging combined (monsterbox.log grows ~1.3 MB/day).
findings.failure_scenario: Steady SD wear on every node, every day, show or no show; a power cut mid-write truncates the file (silently reset to [] on next read). This is the hidden write path that ages SD cards toward the corruption failures Mina already exhibits.
findings.fix: Append NDJSON with periodic compaction, or buffer in RAM and flush hourly via services/atomicStore.js writeJsonAtomic; consider shorter retention.
findings.blast_radius: Every node in the fleet, continuously.
findings.characters_affected: all live nodes (2, 3, 4 now; 1, 5 when powered)

findings.title: A wedged-but-alive server can never auto-recover: exceptions swallowed, no watchdog, Restart downgraded to on-failure
findings.evidence: server.js:74-80 swallows all uncaughtException/unhandledRejection (log-and-continue). /etc/systemd/system/monsterbox.service.d/10-priority.conf silently overrides the base unit's Restart=always to Restart=on-failure (systemctl show confirms Restart=on-failure), and grep finds WatchdogSec in no unit file. No external health-check timer exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Hour nine of a show: a swallowed exception leaves state corrupted or the event loop blocked; systemd sees 'active (running)' forever, no restart ever fires, every endpoint times out, and the show stays dead until someone SSHes in. Hard power-cut recovery is otherwise clean (PID guard verified correct incl. pre-boot mtime and PID-reuse cmdline checks).
findings.fix: Add WatchdogSec=60 + sd_notify keepalive from the event loop (or a systemd timer curling /health with systemctl restart on failure); reconcile the Restart= intent in one drop-in and codify all drop-ins in install.sh like the journald/logrotate blocks.
findings.blast_radius: Whole node; the only failure class with no automatic path back to a running show.

findings.title: characters.json and the tts-config file class are written non-atomically (power-loss corruption)
findings.evidence: saveCharacters uses plain fs.writeFile for data/characters.json (line 136), as do lines 181/193 (audio config, microphones.json) and services/aiConfigStore.js:36 (the tts-config class — the same file class with the live clobber bug). By contrast parts.json/poses.json/scenes.json/app-config/jaw config all correctly route through services/atomicStore.js writeJsonAtomic (verified by grep).
findings.failure_scenario: Power cut mid-write (Mina has ALREADY had hard power-loss events) tears the fleet character registry or a tts-config: server boots with a JSON parse error, falls back to defaults, wrong voice or missing characters on show night — and a torn tts-config is indistinguishable from the known clobber bug, wasting diagnosis time.
findings.fix: Route characterService.js:136/181/193, aiConfigStore.js:36 (and secondarily nodeDiscoveryService.js:131, goblinManagerService.js:82, goblinPlaylistService.js:48, sceneAnalyticsService.js:195) through writeJsonAtomic.
findings.blast_radius: Fleet registry and per-character voice config on every node.
findings.characters_affected: all (registry is fleet-wide); Mina highest risk

findings.title: 53% of the runtime log is per-servo-move debug logging (3 lines per command)
findings.evidence: Frequency analysis of /var/log/monsterbox.log: 13,699 each of '🦷 Servo route: ...' (index.js:696), 'Calling moveToAngle...' and 'moveToAngle completed' = 41,097 of 77,273 total lines; PriorityManager claim/deny churn adds ~5,700 more. Idle loop and head tracking emit these continuously all show.
findings.failure_scenario: Continuous small-block SD writes all night plus real failures buried in noise; log window shrinks (10M rotation fills faster), losing post-mortem evidence after a bad night.
findings.fix: Demote the per-move trio and PriorityManager routine claim/deny lines behind an MB_DEBUG_SERVO env flag.
findings.blast_radius: SD wear and diagnosability on every node.

findings.title: /tmp lives on the SD card and crontab backups accumulate unboundedly (140 files now)
findings.evidence: findmnt shows no tmpfs on /tmp (ext4 root). scheduleService.js:99 writes os.tmpdir()/monsterbox-crontab-<Date.now()>.bak on every crontab change and never deletes; 140 such files counted in /tmp this session, plus /tmp/dl.mp3.
findings.failure_scenario: Unbounded slow growth and SD writes for every schedule edit; after months, clutter and wear with zero recovery value beyond the last backup.
findings.fix: Keep only the last N (e.g. 5) backups on write; and add a tmpfs /tmp mount to the node baseline/install.sh (8 GB RAM, only 1.7 used).

findings.title: Motion-tracker spawn churn: 144 kill/respawn cycles at ~2.4 s CPU each (cv2 import)
findings.evidence: 143 'Motion tracking process exited with code 0' + 1 'code null' in the current log window; measured `python3 -c "import cv2"` = 2.42 s on this Pi (paid on every startMotionTrackingProcess), plus background-subtractor relearn frames. Cycle count correlates with lurk sleep/wake (115 sleep / 113 wake log lines). Process reaping, SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation and stdio draining are all correct (lines 307-345, 389-427).
findings.failure_scenario: Each lurk wake pays 2.4+ s of one core before the head can track, delaying the scare; the churn multiplies CPU spikes during the busiest moments of the show.
findings.fix: Keep the tracker process warm across lurk sleep (pause frame processing via a stdin command) instead of kill/respawn, or accept the cost knowingly — lifecycle correctness itself is fine.
findings.blast_radius: Head-tracking responsiveness and CPU spikes on nodes using lurk mode.

findings.title: express.json/urlencoded body limit is 50 MB
findings.evidence: app.use(express.json({ limit: '50mb' })); app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true, limit: '50mb' })); (lines 242-243). Outbound fleet HTTP is fine (orchestrationService uses AbortController + timeouts on every audited call); sync reads on hot paths are negligible (only scheduleRoutes.js:86 on a cold path).
findings.failure_scenario: Any LAN client (or a buggy fleet peer) POSTs tens of MB of JSON; the Pi buffers and JSON.parses it on the event loop, stalling scene execution and jaw sync for seconds.
findings.fix: Drop the global limit to 1-5 MB; give any genuinely large endpoint (audio upload uses multipart already) a per-route limit.
findings.blast_radius: Momentary whole-app stalls under accidental or hostile large bodies.

findings.title: ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm start keeps a 60 MB npm wrapper resident and adds a signal-forwarding hop
findings.evidence: ps shows npm wrapper PID 27346 RSS 60,176 KB alive beside node server.js (124 MB) for the life of the service; unit file ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm start. gracefulShutdown (server.js ~958-1052) is correct, but SIGTERM must transit npm first.
findings.failure_scenario: Wasted RAM per node and one more layer where a shutdown signal can be mishandled after an npm upgrade; also skews MemoryCurrent accounting.
findings.fix: ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /home/remote/MonsterBox/server.js in the unit (codify in install.sh).
findings.blast_radius: ~60 MB RAM per node; marginal shutdown risk.

findings.title: Goblin reconnect loop polls storage nodes forever every 30 s
findings.evidence: startHeartbeatMonitor setInterval plus a 30 s reconnect cycle (comment at line 567); 605 throttled 'Attempting to reconnect 3 offline goblins' lines in monsterbox.log. Offline is EXPECTED for the storage nodes.
findings.failure_scenario: Perpetual failed network attempts and log lines against nodes that are intentionally powered off; noise, not outage.
findings.fix: Add an expectedOffline/storage flag per goblin that suppresses reconnect attempts, or back off exponentially to minutes.

unverified: Camera CPU at 1920x1080@30 was not measured (would have required changing the live stream); only the VGA15 cost (~0.6% of one core while actively streamed) was measured directly.
goblin/goblin-pi.js:222 behavior verified by code only — the goblin Pi3B nodes are offline, so the ffplay scale cost was not measured on real hardware.
No production source of SIGHUP or clean exit-0 was found, so the Restart=on-failure downgrade (10-priority.conf) leaving the service down after a clean exit is a latent gap, not a demonstrated one.
Steady-state size of performance-history.json at full 30-day retention is unknown; 1.48 MB is the measured current size and it is still growing.

Health items verified GOOD and needing no work: PID guard (singleInstance.js) correct in all examined cases including PID reuse; journald 64M cap and logrotate ARE live AND now codified in install.sh:489-496 (the memory note that they are not in git is stale); atomicStore used correctly for parts/poses/scenes/app-config/jaw; orchestration outbound HTTP has timeouts; mpg123/pw-play/MJPEG-proxy cleanup handlers correct; hardwareService/exec.js has 30s timeout + SIGKILL with drained stdio.
The task brief said 73 motion-tracker restarts; the current log window actually contains 144 tracker exits (143 code 0, 1 code null).
